rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the full elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Hold the gradient fixed and raise temperature to probe selectivity of the single critical pair. The other pairs have resolution headroom, and the last peak currently elutes comfortably before 10 minutes.

The central peak pattern suggests an elution-order crossover between 40 and 50 °C, so a further 5 °C increase may separate the critical pair. Keep the gradient unchanged to assess this while monitoring the neighboring pair whose resolution decreased at 50 °C.

Injection 3 reached the maximum CRF of 1.000; retain it as the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method, checking the two pairs that were just above R = 1.5.

The shorter gradient sacrificed resolution, so restore the successful 12-minute duration and raise the starting organic fraction by one step. This tests whether a narrower gradient window can shorten retention while preserving full resolution; injection 3 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

With the maximum-score method secured at injection 3, test a substantially faster regime. Higher temperature and a steeper gradient may carry the troublesome middle pair through an elution-order crossover and restore separation on the other side.

Test the cooler selectivity regime with a 10-minute gradient, seeking full resolution faster than injection 3. The temperature-dependent central peak pattern suggests that cooling may separate the critical cluster on the opposite side of its elution-order crossovers.

Test an intermediate cooler temperature: 25 °C produced several co-elutions, while 40 °C left only one unresolved pair with the 12-minute gradient. This probes whether 35 °C separates the central cluster while retaining the time advantage of a 10-minute gradient; injection 3 remains the benchmark.

Return to the successful 55 °C selectivity and narrow the organic window. The shallower slope should help the marginal middle pair, while the higher starting organic fraction may shorten retention; monitor early-peak compression as well.

At the same starting composition and temperature, injection 5 narrowly missed full resolution. Lowering its endpoint to 0.85 makes the gradient shallower and may restore that pair while keeping the last peak under 10 minutes, providing a more robust maximum-score alternative.

With two maximum-score methods secured, probe a faster, higher-organic regime at 60 °C. This tests whether the central peaks separate beyond their selectivity crossover, while checking for compression of the earliest pair.

Increase starting organic by one step to test whether the unresolved middle pair separates further in this fast, high-temperature regime. Watch the earliest pair closely because its resolution may fall as the starting strength increases; retain injection 3 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Test whether the narrower organic window at 40 °C separates the central cluster differently from the broad gradient, which had only one unresolved pair. This explores an alternative selectivity regime while retaining injection 3 as the proven maximum-score method.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 40 °C changes the central elution order enough to open a faster resolved regime. Injection 3 already secures the maximum CRF, so this run explores a substantial time reduction rather than incremental score improvement.

Refine between the successful 12-minute gradient and the unresolved 10-minute gradient at 55 °C by lowering the latter’s endpoint. This gives a slope only slightly steeper than injection 3, testing a modest retention-time reduction while preserving the critical pair.

Back off the slope from injection 15 by lowering the endpoint one grid step. This restores injection 3’s successful slope in a shorter programmed gradient, targeting full resolution without increasing the last-peak time.

Refine the promising 40 °C regime from injection 13 with a higher starting fraction and a shallower slope, aiming to lift its sole unresolved pair above 1.5. Monitor early-pair compression and the 10-minute last-peak threshold; the maximum-score methods remain secured.

Test a shallower gradient at 60 °C to recover separation of the temperature-sensitive middle pair while retaining the stronger separation of the other critical pair. This targets a maximum-score alternative with more resolution margin, though the last peak may approach the 10-minute threshold.

Bracket the resolution boundary between injections 5 and 10 by testing their intermediate endpoint. This may retain full resolution while reducing the 8.00-minute last-peak time of injection 10; injection 3 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method.

Use a slope between injections 10 and 19 to recover the marginal pair while shortening retention relative to injection 10. This targets another fully resolved, maximum-score method with a shorter programmed gradient.

Shorten the programmed gradient to 8 minutes while preserving the successful slope of injections 3 and 16. All peaks should elute before the endpoint reaches the column outlet, testing a lower-solvent method expected to retain the maximum CRF.

Test one step shallower than injection 10 to increase the middle-pair resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. The fastest proven fully resolved method remains injection 3; this run seeks a less marginal maximum-score alternative.

Refine injection 9 by lowering its endpoint to improve the unresolved middle pair, while its other critical pair had R = 1.76. This targets a maximum-score alternative with greater minimum-resolution margin, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one grid step from injection 23 to lift its sole marginal pair above R = 1.5. The last peak has about 1.5 minutes of headroom before the time penalty, making this a promising route to a maximum-score method with improved resolution margin.

Use a slightly steeper slope than injection 24 to reduce retention while aiming to preserve its improved resolution margin. Injection 3 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method; this final run refines the better-separated alternative.
